title: Define management and describe the management process and the functions of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling
Explain why management is important to an organisation
Compare the schools of management thought: classical, neoclassical or behavioural, quantitative, systems, contingency and contemporary (total quality management and the learning organisation)
Describe the challenges and opportunities facing management: business models, information explosion, managing change, globalisation and environmental sustainability
Explain strategic management: strategy and plan, types of strategy, vision and mission, the elements and phases of strategic management and its benefits
Explain business environment analysis and why a manager must understand the external environment
Explain what planning is, the steps in the planning process and why planning is important
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of planning
Explain management by objectives: the MBO process, SMART goals, limitations and advantages

Describe the components of a plan, including environmental analysis (PESTLE and SWOT), internal analysis tools, fixation of objectives, planning premises, evaluation of alternatives and finalisation of the plan
Explain contingency planning and what a contingency plan covers
Explain forecasting (long, medium and short term) and decision making, including group decisions, conditions of decision making and principles of decision making
Explain organising, why it is important and the stages and steps of the organising process
Describe the principles of organising: specialisation, authority, chain of command, unity of command, delegation and span of control
Compare centralised and decentralised organisations and describe their advantages and disadvantages
Describe line and staff, functional and committee organisations with their advantages and disadvantages
Distinguish formal and informal organisation and describe their features, advantages and disadvantages
Explain organisation charts and manuals, their types, advantages and disadvantages
Describe types of organisational culture and the relationship between authority and responsibility, including sources and forms of authority
Identify the key issues in organisation structure: turnover, productivity, process management, role specification, customer relationships, innovation and teamwork
Explain organisational change, resistance to change and the change management models (Lewin, McKinsey 7S, Kotter, Nudge, ADKAR, Bridges, Kubler-Ross)
Explain conflict dynamics, conflict management skills and the five strategies for conflict resolution
Explain the functions, objectives, nature and salient features of staffing, its facets and its significance
Describe the systems approach to staffing and the factors affecting the number and type of managers needed
Explain recruitment: types, stages and the method for successful recruitment
Describe the selection process and its importance
Explain training: importance, benefits and types
Explain retention and development of staff: effective practices, strategies, implementation and common problems
Explain knowledge and learning management, including the SECI model
Explain performance appraisal: types, objectives, advantages, disadvantages, methods, BARS and key result areas
Explain human resource development, managing generations and diversity, industrial relations, management of change, career strategy and stress management
